- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts rise steadily, cap the upward slope to avoid overshoot after recent spikes.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and true prices show sharp declines, adjust forecast downward by 2–5% relative to prior peak to account for mean reversion.  
- After high-event periods (e.g., 20+ auctions), model forecasts tend to overestimate short-term volatility; reduce forecast volatility by 15–30% for 30d horizon.  
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, forecast should not rise above 10–15% above recent 7-day average to avoid lagged overreaction.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should not assume linear trend; apply smoothing or exponential decay to avoid false momentum.  
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, reduce forecast mean by 3–8% relative to historical 30d mean to reflect policy-induced downward pressure.
